issues.display_title: Issue #209: Environment-Based Redis Cache Prefix Isolation
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Environment-Based Redis Cache Prefix Isolation

Files Changed

  • src/lib/redis/keys.go
  • src/lib/redis/redis.go
  • src/lib/redis/keys_test.go (new)

Resolution Strategy

  1. Dynamic Prefix Resolution: Replaced static "villume-api" string with a dynamic resolver function getPrefix() and an initializer InitRedisPrefix().
  2. Format Rule: Uses villume-api-{{APP_ENV}}. When APP_ENV is unset or empty, it defaults safely to "development", resulting in villume-api-development.
  3. Key Methods Migration: Updated all key-generation and pattern-generation methods on cacheKeys to utilize getPrefix() dynamically.
  4. Startup Initialization: Added InitRedisPrefix() invocation to redis.Connect() so the prefix reflects .env configurations loaded at boot.

Code Changes

1. Dynamic Prefix Implementation (src/lib/redis/keys.go)

var RedisPrefix = "villume-api-development"

func init() {
	InitRedisPrefix()
}

// InitRedisPrefix configures RedisPrefix using APP_ENV as villume-api-{{APP_ENV}}.
func InitRedisPrefix() {
	RedisPrefix = getPrefix()
}

func getPrefix() string {
	appEnv := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("APP_ENV")))
	if appEnv == "" {
		appEnv = "development"
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("villume-api-%s", appEnv)
}

func (k cacheKeys) UserDetail(identifier string, version ...int) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s:user:v%d:detail:%s", getPrefix(), getVersion(version), identifier)
}

func (k cacheKeys) UserUsername(identifier string, version ...int) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s:user:v%d:username:%s", getPrefix(), getVersion(version), identifier)
}

// ... all other key and pattern methods use getPrefix()

2. Startup Hook (src/lib/redis/redis.go)

func Connect() {
	InitRedisPrefix()

	addrsLine := os.Getenv("REDIS_ADDRS")
	// ...
}

Behavior

  • User Detail Cache:
    • Development (APP_ENV=development): villume-api-development:user:v1:detail:<encrypt>
    • Live (APP_ENV=live): villume-api-live:user:v1:detail:<encrypt>
    • Production (APP_ENV=production): villume-api-production:user:v1:detail:<encrypt>
  • Cross-Environment Collision Prevention: Even when Dev and Live share identical Redis connection details and cloned databases with identical user encrypt tokens, their cache keys are completely isolated.
  • Pattern Deletion Safety: Pattern deletions such as BillingCardPattern only match and delete keys under villume-api-<current_env>:billing:*, preventing accidental cache clearing across environments.

Verification

go test -v ./src/lib/redis/...

Expected result:

=== RUN   TestRedisPrefixConfiguration
=== RUN   TestRedisPrefixConfiguration/uses_APP_ENV_when_set_to_development
=== RUN   TestRedisPrefixConfiguration/uses_APP_ENV_when_set_to_production
=== RUN   TestRedisPrefixConfiguration/uses_APP_ENV_when_set_to_live
=== RUN   TestRedisPrefixConfiguration/fallback_when_APP_ENV_is_unset
=== RUN   TestRedisPrefixConfiguration/patterns_correctly_reflect_prefix
--- PASS: TestRedisPrefixConfiguration (0.00s)
PASS

Overview

Redis is utilized across multiple services in the backend for caching, including user personal details (GET /v1/users/detail), usernames, product billing, coupons, and room listings. Previously, the cache key prefix was hardcoded as "villume-api" across all environments in src/lib/redis/keys.go.

Problem

  1. Cross-Environment Collision: When Development and Live environments share the same Redis instance (or same Redis DB index 0), cache keys with the same identifier collided.
  2. Account Discrepancy on Cloned Databases: When production databases are cloned/dumped to dev for testing, user accounts (such as villumesupport) share the same encrypt value (sub claim in JWT). As a result, an authenticated user in Dev calling /v1/users/detail received cached Live user profile data (or vice versa).
  3. Cross-Environment Cache Invalidation: Deleting a cache key or executing pattern deletions (e.g. BillingCardPattern, BillingCouponPattern) from Dev cleared or affected corresponding cache entries in Production.

Goals

  1. Namespace all Redis keys dynamically with villume-api-{{APP_ENV}}.
    • APP_ENV=development -> villume-api-development
    • APP_ENV=production -> villume-api-production
    • APP_ENV=live -> villume-api-live
  2. Default to villume-api-development if APP_ENV is unset or empty.
  3. Automatically update RedisPrefix during application startup (redis.Connect()).
  4. Ensure pattern matching deletions (DeletePattern) are strictly confined to the active environment.
  5. Provide automated unit tests verifying prefix behavior across different environments.

Scope

In scope:

  • src/lib/redis/keys.go (implement dynamic getPrefix() and InitRedisPrefix(), update key methods)
  • src/lib/redis/redis.go (trigger InitRedisPrefix() in Connect())
  • src/lib/redis/keys_test.go (unit tests for prefix configuration)

Implementation

Please see the implementation document here: Implementation Document

issues.display_title: Issue #210: Dynamic Storage Directory for Support Blog Image Uploads
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Dynamic Storage Directory for Support Blog Image Uploads

Files Changed

  • src/action/v1/blog/helpers.go
  • src/action/v1/blog/helpers_test.go
  • src/action/v1/blog/supportUploadImage.go
  • src/action/v1/blog/supportUploadImage_test.go

Resolution Strategy

  1. Helper Function (GetBlogFolder): Added a helper that inspects os.Getenv("APP_ENV"). If it equals "development" or "dev", it returns "blog-dev", otherwise it returns "blog-live".
  2. Directory Resolution: Updated SupportUploadImage to resolve target directories using filepath.Join(baseDir, folder) instead of hardcoding "blog".
  3. Robust Error Handling: Added explicit error checks and server logs if os.MkdirAll or c.SaveFile encounters filesystem permission or I/O failures.
  4. Asset URL Alignment: Formatted the output URL to reference /v1/asset/<folder>/<filename>.

Code Changes

1. Helper Function (src/action/v1/blog/helpers.go)

// GetBlogFolder returns "blog-dev" if APP_ENV is development, otherwise "blog-live".
func GetBlogFolder() string {
	appEnv := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("APP_ENV")))
	if appEnv == "development" || appEnv == "dev" {
		return "blog-dev"
	}
	return "blog-live"
}

2. Upload Action (src/action/v1/blog/supportUploadImage.go)

	folder := GetBlogFolder()
	blogDir := filepath.Join(baseDir, folder)
	if err := os.MkdirAll(blogDir, 0o755); err != nil {
		log.Printf("❌ Failed to create upload directory %s: %v", blogDir, err)
		return helpers.SendError(c, helpers.ErrorOpts{
			Status:   fiber.StatusInternalServerError,
			Messages: "Failed to create upload directory: " + err.Error(),
		})
	}

	filename, err := helpers.RandomHexFilename(ext)
	if err != nil {
		return helpers.SendError(c, helpers.ErrorOpts{Status: fiber.StatusInternalServerError, Messages: "Failed to generate filename: " + err.Error()})
	}
	dst := filepath.Join(blogDir, filename)
	if err := c.SaveFile(fileHeader, dst); err != nil {
		log.Printf("❌ Failed to save uploaded file to %s: %v", dst, err)
		return helpers.SendError(c, helpers.ErrorOpts{
			Status:   fiber.StatusInternalServerError,
			Messages: "Failed to save file: " + err.Error(),
		})
	}

	appURL := strings.TrimRight(os.Getenv("APP_URL"), "/")
	var imageURL string
	if appURL != "" {
		imageURL = fmt.Sprintf("%s/v1/asset/%s/%s", appURL, folder, filename)
	} else {
		imageURL = fmt.Sprintf("/v1/asset/%s/%s", folder, filename)
	}

Behavior

  • In APP_ENV=development or dev, files are uploaded to <baseDir>/blog-dev/<filename> and returned with URL /v1/asset/blog-dev/<filename>.
  • In production/live environments, files are stored under <baseDir>/blog-live/<filename> and served from /v1/asset/blog-live/<filename>.
  • Filesystem errors now yield HTTP 500 with descriptive error messages instead of silent failure.

Verification

go test -v ./src/action/v1/blog -run "TestGetBlogFolder|TestSupportUploadImage"

Expected result:

=== RUN   TestGetBlogFolder
--- PASS: TestGetBlogFolder (0.00s)
=== RUN   TestSupportUploadImage_FileTooLarge
--- PASS: TestSupportUploadImage_FileTooLarge (0.00s)
=== RUN   TestSupportUploadImage_DynamicDirectory
--- PASS: TestSupportUploadImage_DynamicDirectory (0.01s)
PASS

Overview

The support admin blog management features include an image upload endpoint (POST /v1/support/blog/upload-image) used for article cover photos and inline Editor.js images. Previously, images were stored directly into a static /blog folder under the configured asset/image directory (DIRECTORY_IMAGES or DIRECTORY_ASSET, fallback uploads/blog).

Problem

  1. Asset Collision Risk: When Development/Staging and Production/Live share storage volumes or bucket mounts, uploading images in dev could accidentally overwrite or intermingle with production article images.
  2. Environment Contamination: Development mock images and test artifacts remained mixed with production content in the same directory.
  3. Missing Granular Error Diagnostics: Previous file operations silently failed or lacked detailed error context when folder creation or file saving failed.

Goals

  1. Implement dynamic directory resolution based on the APP_ENV environment variable:
    • APP_ENV=development or dev -> saves into blog-dev/
    • Production / other environments -> saves into blog-live/
  2. Update the public image asset URL returned in the response to correctly reference the environment folder.
  3. Improve error reporting for directory creation (os.MkdirAll) and file writing (c.SaveFile).
  4. Maintain full compatibility with Editor.js Image Tool response contracts.
  5. Provide comprehensive unit tests covering all environment scenarios.

Scope

In scope:

  • src/action/v1/blog/helpers.go (implement GetBlogFolder helper)
  • src/action/v1/blog/helpers_test.go (unit tests for folder resolution)
  • src/action/v1/blog/supportUploadImage.go (integrate dynamic directory and error logging)
  • src/action/v1/blog/supportUploadImage_test.go (test upload handler with different environments)

Implementation

Please see the implementation document here: Implementation Document
